you're set for life.

One last lesson: when you're in a pinch, calm down
first, and then carefully think things over.
And don't worry. You'll do just fine on your own."
Sensei smiles happily.
A gust of wind blows.
The grass sways in unison.
Sensei is no longer there.
"Bye-bye... Sensei."
I say, realizing that I will never see her again.

All that remains are the words she left behind, and
these strange glasses.

I only knew her for seven days, but she taught me the
most important thing of all.
As I stand there in a daze, tears well up in my eyes.
―――Ah, what a fool I am.
All I did was say goodbye.
I never once said thank you.
I'm discharged from the hospital soon after.

When I leave, I'm not sent back to the Tohno mansion,
but to another house.

Although my body has recovered, I'm still suffering
from the aftereffects of the accident. I am no longer
wanted by the Tohno family.
But that's okay.
Tohno Shiki will do fine on his own.
I will lead a new life with a new family.

I leave the hospital room where I spent my tenth
summer.
The curtains are still fluttering.
I squint once again at the blue sky.
A light breeze heralds the end of summer.

Unfortunately, I don't have anything to talk to her
about.

She keeps on smiling, not seeming to mind the fact that
I'm at a loss for words.
"Um... do you go to school by train, Senpai?"
"Well, yes. I use it when I have to.

What about you, Tohno-kun? Is your house far from
here?"

"Yeah, it's pretty far. I get on at the end of the
line.

Or, I used to at least. Today's the last time I take
the train to school."
"Oh my. Are you moving?"

I can't think of a good way to explain it, so I just
hand-wave the details.

My gaze drifts over to the window and I look out at the
view of the city.

Ciel-senpai must have picked up on the fact that I
found the topic a little difficult to discuss, because
she graciously refrains from prying further.

Our mundane conversation carries on for fifteen
minutes.

Before long, the train arrives at our destination:
Souya Station.
It's just before seven o'clock.

It's a little early for school, and the city is still
asleep. The area in front of the station is quiet now,
but in an hour, it'll be full of people and cars.
"I guess this is where we part ways.

Thanks for keeping me company. If you see me at school,
please don't hesitate to say hello, okay?"
Senpai smiles and waves back at me as she runs off.

She's so lively that I feel like running as well, but
I'm not in any particular rush.

I have my health to worry about, so I decide to go to
school at my normal pace.
Still... I'm curious.

It isn't the bag on her shoulder that's caught my eye,
though――it's the pair of legs that have slipped into
view.

The splendid sweep of her legs is the embodiment――no,
the very  of vivacious energy.

Though still, they manifest the lively motion of
smoothly flowing water.

This is what I would call beauty in form. I can't look
away. In fact, forget looking away――I'm actively
being drawn in.
"Um... Tohno-kun?"

Then, I realize that beauty and strength go hand in
hand.

Her legs are quite plump, but the truth is, these are
the legs of a sprinter.

I heard through the grapevine that at the physical
fitness test the other day, she beat out the track team
to set a new record for our school. These are legs that
can run a hundred meters in thirteen seconds... I'm
struck by the sense that I'm gazing at a living gem.

"Um, you know, your face is very close to my... and the
movement of your hands..."
"I'm sorry. This matter is of the utmost importance."
"I-I see... Of the utmost importance, you say..."

Alas, the sad truth of the matter is I'm neither her
trainer nor a rival athlete.

Even if I were to somehow obtain the secret of speed
itself, there's no way I could suddenly master the art
of running.

"Ah, no, but you see, I have absolutely no idea  is
so important!"
"Well of course. I don't understand either."

How can I put into words the psychology of being
attracted to something beautiful?

Then again, isn't there something wrong if we can't
adequately describe beauty? If we can't honestly admit
that something is beautiful?

When will human beings be able to transcend all
prejudices and discrimination, and talk about the
essence of things?
"T-Tohno-kun, are you alright?!
Something just hit you on the head?!"
"Yeah... I'll survive, just about."

With the side of my head still smarting from the
impact, I pick up the object that has fallen onto the
seat.

It's a palm-sized lump of metal that sparkles
lustrously.
Pretty clearly just a smartphone.
"Excuse me. Did something fly over here?"

"I guess you mean this... It came in at a pretty
incredible angle. Do you have an app that lets you fly
it around like that?"
"Are you an idiot? Thank you very much."

The girl takes the phone as if nothing had happened,
and walks over to a door one row of seats away.

We stare at each other, reeling from what just
happened.
After a moment's confusion, I come back to my senses.
I clear my throat to break the tension.
"I'm sorry, I got a little distracted.

More importantly, is something the matter? You aren't
in any clubs, right Senpai? Why are you heading to
school this early?"

"Well, to tell you the truth, I'm on my way back from
volunteering.

You see, the student council asked for volunteers to
pick up trash in the park, right? That's what I was
doing until just now."
Aha. That explanation makes total sense.

Our attractively bespectacled Senpai is always working
hard for the sake of others.

"It was just a thirty-minute early morning volunteer
activity.

Everyone else went back home for a while, but I thought
I'd just go straight to school because heading home
first would've been too much trouble."
The bag on Senpai's shoulder makes a clanking sound.

I thought it was something for her club activities, but
it seems to be cleaning equipment.

"Oh my. Do you want to see what's inside? You seem so
innocent on the outside, but you're really dying to
rummage through your Senpai's belongings... how bold!"
Senpai leans in close to look me in the eye.

Wait... her face, her body, and so many other things
are so close that I'm not even sure where to look.

"N-No, that's not it, I just thought that if you had a
foldable broom or a rake, that would be unusual..."

", I see. You also want to see my all-purpose
long-range pruning shears, do you? Very well. In that
case, come by the tea ceremony club after school.
You're more than welcome."

I can't help but feel embarrassed, hearing her say that
with an infectious smile spread across her face.

Unable to come up with a witty reply, the best I can
muster is a weak 'yes'.

I don't know where the tea ceremony club room is, but I
can find that out later.

"It's a promise, then. Just between you and me, I've
purchased a surplus of snacks using the club funds.
They don't exactly have a great shelf life, so I need a
healthy boy to help me out."

"I-Is that so? Well, if my schedule permits, I'll
definitely come.

Although, getting lured in by food almost makes it seem
like I'm a cat."

Her smile is so friendly that I can't help but joke a
little.
The upperclassman with the green ribbon replies―――
"It's more like a puppy, I think.

I mean, felines are awful. Dutiful and intelligent
canines are the ones you can truly count on in the
end!"

She declares her oddly strong preferences with a
pleased look on her face.

Since we're headed the same way, our conversation
continues to roll on.
We talk about last week's midterm exams.

About the sports festival, which was reduced in scale
and only lasted a day.
About the cafeteria, where the menu has never changed.

About the controversy between the students and the
school over the use of mobile devices, which makes us
both sigh, so we change the topic and laugh about our
impressions of a movie we had recently seen.
Fifteen minutes pass quickly.

This is the universally beloved Senpai that the rumors
describe――she can really hold a conversation.

I don't want to think about the fact we'll soon arrive
at Souya Station, so I raise another topic.
―――But.
"Hey... you're making too much noise."

As she points out, we had forgotten about our
surroundings.
We both bow our heads to apologize.
"We got told off, huh..."
"Sorry...
I was laughing too loud, I guess."
After that, the conversation peters out.

It's like the friendly atmosphere we had experienced up
until now had been a lie.

Everyone is just a stranger, and a silence peculiar to
the city dominates the train.
The train arrives at Souya Station.
It's just before seven o'clock.

It's a little early for school, and the city is still
asleep.

The station is quiet now, but in an hour, it will be
full of people and cars.

"There's not much traffic this morning either. It feels
like the city is slow to wake up lately. I wonder if
everyone is staying up late."

Senpai says something strange while carrying her heavy
luggage.

"Um... would you like me to take your luggage to
school?"

"Huh? Ah, no, no, don't worry about it. I have a stop
to make, so I'll leave you here."
Senpai smiles and waves back at me as she runs off.

She's so fast and light on her feet that she reminds me
of a frolicking gazelle.

I feel like running along with her, but I have no
particular reason to hurry.

Besides, I have my body to worry about. I'll just head
to school at my usual pace.
And then...
The girl from earlier comes out of the ticket gate.
She brushes past me at a fast pace―――
"You're like an animal.

Don't you feel embarrassed to be acting like that in
public?"
―――And leaves behind some scathing criticism.

It's lunch break, and the corridor is filled with a
jumble of students headed this way and that.

Most of them are on their way to the cafeteria, but
some are going to visit their friends' classes with
lunchboxes in hand, or making their way to the
courtyard or the gym.

Losing myself in the crowd, I wonder if I should have a
proper lunch in the cafeteria or just buy a sandwich or
something at the store.

At the end of the corridor, I see the familiar figure
of Senpai.
Is it my imagination?
Or is she coming straight toward me...?
"Thank goodness. I've been looking for you, Tohno-kun.

You've saved me the trouble of having to visit your
classroom."
"W-Well, that's great. Good to see you, Ciel-senpai."

For some reason, I feel embarrassed and reply with a
lackluster greeting.
"Yes, good to see you too.

Although, we've already met today, so 'good to see you'
isn't the right phrase."
"Oh... yeah. I guess you're right."
I look away, feeling more and more embarrassed.
Why is that I wonder...?

I should be used to talking to Senpai, but today I'm
unusually conscious of her. I wonder if it's because
she saw me absorbed in my thoughts this morning.

"Tohno-kun...? You seem somewhat restless, are you in a
hurry or something?"
"No, I'm not in a hurry. Not at all."

I can't just admit to her that I'm fascinated by every
little move she makes.

"Anyway, Senpai, you said you were looking for me. Is
there something I can help you with?"

"Yes. I'm sure I caused you some trouble this morning,
didn't I?

I wanted to apologize for that, so I've been looking
for you."
"Trouble this morning... Ah, you mean on the train?
But that was more of a blessing than a nuisance."
It was fun talking with Ciel-senpai.

I felt like the trip to the station just flew by as a
result.

"Well, but we got yelled at by that one girl for being
noisy.

That's what I'm apologizing for. If you don't mind me
asking, were you on your way to get lunch?"

"Yes. I was trying to decide if I should go to the
cafeteria or just buy something."

"Great, then let me join you. Let's go to the
cafeteria. I'll treat you to make up for what happened
this morning."
"Huh?"

With a smile on her face, Senpai grabs my arm and
starts walking.

A third-year student standing in the second-years'
hallway is already enough to stand out, but this is
really going to turn some heads.

All of the students in the hallway are looking our way
and busily whispering amongst themselves.
"W-Wait a minute!

What happened this morning was my fault, so there's no
need for you to apologize! In fact, it's the other way
around.  should be the one apologizing!"

Realizing that I'm blushing, I extricate myself from
Senpai's arm.

". I can't ignore that. You're the one who should be
apologizing? What I'm hearing is that you'll do me a
favor as punishment, right?"

Her teasing glances make my already red cheeks even
redder.
"No, that was just a figure of speech."
"Then give it up and let me take you to the cafeteria.

I'm in the mood to have lunch with someone. Consider it
bad luck and let me treat you."
That's just unfair...

If someone smiles at me like that, I can't possibly say
no.

"... You're going to treat me? You've got it all
backwards, Senpai."

"I mean it, I really enjoyed talking to you on the
train.
So let's hurry to the cafeteria!
If we don't, there won't be any free seats left!"

Ciel-senpai takes my hand again and walks briskly down
the corridor.

We must have beaten the crowds, as there are plenty of
open tables in the cafeteria.

Though there is a sizable queue at the counter already,
it shouldn't take more than about... five minutes or so
to order.

"I'll go get in line. Tohno-kun, please save a seat for
me. Is there any food you don't like? If so, you should
tell me now."
"Nope, none. I'm not really a picky eater."
"That is excellent news.
Well then, I'll be back in a flash!"

Without waiting for my reply, Ciel-senpai gets in line
to order.

I guess I'll have to accept that I'm being treated to
lunch today.

"Vacant seats for two... if possible, seats in a corner
would be nice..."

I'm not sure if my mind can handle this whole situation
of having lunch with Ciel-senpai.

If I am going to have lunch with her, I'd prefer to sit
in a place where we can't be seen by many people.

Looking around the cafeteria, I see that there are some
empty seats in the middle, but the corner seats are
already occupied by other students' belongings.

At this hour, there are no corner seats for two
people―――
"Oh――there's one."

However, the table is about to be occupied by a
familiar face.
"Yo, Tohno, c'mere c'mere."

An orange-haired delinquent is waving his hand in the
air, with no regard at all for the stares of the people
around him. What a headache.

That said, ignoring him would be rude and there are no
other empty corner seats available.

In a way, he is a man who can keep people away. I
suppose it's my duty as his friend to take advantage of
his useful qualities.

"You're late. Didn't I tell you there'd be a special
guest today? Quit acting like the world revolves around
your schedule."
"Ah, I remember you saying something like that.
So, where is this special guest?"

"Mmm, that's the thing. It's been on the schedule since
yesterday, but she canceled on me this morning.
Something about how 'I'm busy at lunch today because
there's someone I want to apologize to'."

His shoulders slump in disappointment as he eats his
chikara udon.
"Someone she wants to apologize to?"
That sounds all too familiar.

"This special guest, is she a third-year by any
chance?"

"A short-haired girl who looks good in glasses and is
both restless and cheerful, but still comes off as
dependable?"
"What the hell, since when can you read my thoughts?!"
"No... that's not it, it's just..."
"Sorry for the wait.
Are you sure you want to sit here, Tohno-kun?"
Senpai comes over with a radiant smile.

In her hands, she carries a tray with food for two
people.
"What the hell?!"
"Oh my, it's Inui-kun.
What a coincidence."
Senpai nonchalantly takes a seat at the table.

She chooses the seat opposite me――putting her next to
Arihiko.

Arihiko makes an unfamiliar sound. Perhaps he can't
cope with his sudden good fortune. I know what he's
going through――I felt the same way not too long ago.
"Please help yourself, Tohno-kun.
Don't hesitate to fill up on food today."
There's no way I can say no to a smile like that.
I give up and sit down in the seat facing Ciel-senpai.
"Alright then, thank you very much."

I clasp my hands together and look down at the tray
that Senpai has brought.
On the tray, there was
curry rice,
curry rice,

and
curry udon.
Wait, what??
"Um, Senpai...?"
"Yes? What is it, Tohno-kun?"
"No, this――what is the meaning of this?"

"What do you mean, it's lunch for you and me. What else
could it be?"
"Yes, but I can only see curry..."
"Of course, it's everyone's favorite, classic curry."

You don't have to tell me that. The problem is that
there is  curry.
"You bought three dishes..."

"Of course. You're a growing boy, so you need to eat
up. I'm fine with just one dish, so please choose
whatever you like."
"Then, I'll have curry rice and curry udon."

Any other combination will just be having the same dish
twice.
"Please don't leave any food behind.
You're not a picky eater, right, Tohno-kun?"
There isn't a trace of malice in her smile.

She isn't joking around or pulling a prank on me here,
she really does have only the best of intentions.
"Thanks for the meal."

I resign myself to my fate and dip my spoon into the
curry rice.
And then.
"Damn you, Tohno-kun!"

The man whose brain malfunctioned a minute ago has
finally rebooted.

"How long are you gonna keep giving your dear best
friend the cold shoulder?! You should be like 'Hey!
Thanks for always being alive, Inui-kun! Oh! By the
way, I should totally introduce you to my beautiful
upperclassman today! Oh no! Something came up! Time to
go to the back of the school, why don't the two of you
have a pleasant chat!' Also, if you have any leftover
curry udon, you can give it to me!"

"You're not getting anything. But thank you for always
being alive, Inui-kun."
Arihiko's arm darts in my direction.

I skillfully guard the curry udon against those evil
hands.
"Huh? Inui-kun, you know Tohno-kun?"

"What are you talkin' about? I don't just  him,
we've been best buds since middle school!"
My so-called 'best bud' reiterates strongly.

"I see. I'm sorry I broke my promise. You see, the
person I caused trouble for this morning was
Tohno-kun."

"It's okay! It's for a good reason. I would've brought
him here myself if you'd told me his name.
So, what bad things did this guy do to you anyway?"

"We bumped into each other on the train early in the
morning, and while we were chatting, another passenger
got angry.

It's all my fault, I should have been more mindful of
the people around us. Tohno-kun didn't do anything
wrong, but he got yelled at because of me."

"Ah, an early morning train? I feel like people have
every right to talk if they want to.

Wait. Early
morning? I know Tohno does, but do you come to school
by train as well?"

"I was on my way back from volunteering this morning.
Picking up trash in the park.

Didn't you see the bulletin board at school? Students
were asked to volunteer."

"Ah, that thing at the seaside park... as expected of
Senpai, thanks for your hard work.

The teachers rely on you because you do stuff like that
though. They'll slack off any chance they get, so I
kinda wish you wouldn't let them get away with it."
"It's okay, I do it because I like it.

Besides, the
teachers are thinking about the school. I don't like
the way you're talking about them, Inui-kun."
Ciel-senpai ruthlessly rebukes Arihiko's lazy opinions.

From the looks of it, he seems to be close to her in
his own way.

"Senpai, do you do volunteer work every day by any
chance?"

"What, you didn't know? Ciel-senpai here is such a
handy person that she's called the true student council

"I know. She's the perfect third-year who can solve

"Yeah. The first-years went and made a whole fan club

the teachers wouldn't complain."

Arihiko sounds so proud you'd think he was talking
about himself.

"I didn't know there was even a fan club... You're
amazing, Ciel-senpai. It's a big deal to be counted on
by our teachers, that's for sure."
I look at Senpai with admiration.
"Ah, yeah. Well, thank you very much."
Senpai stirs her curry rice with a spoon.

I suppose it's to hide her embarrassment, but it also
reminds me of my immediate enemy.

Curry rice isn't the only thing on my plate, I also
have to contend with the curry udon.

Although the doctor has warned me not to eat too much,
I'd feel like I let Senpai down if I didn't finish
eating both.

I guess I'll start with the curry rice, and try to
enjoy it before I start to get too full.

As I eat, Senpai and Arihiko talk about each other's

I knew that Arihiko's parents had passed away, but it
seems that Ciel-senpai is living alone as well.

Apparently her apartment is pretty close to Souya
Station.

It seems that she's renting an apartment in the
residential area to the southeast of the station, next

area to the north.
", I see.
By the way, where do you live, Tohno-kun?"
"Huh?"

As I'm eating curry rice in peace, Senpai suddenly asks
me a question.

"Where do I live? That's a bit of a difficult question

After all, I'll be living somewhere else starting
today.

I don't feel comfortable explaining the situation. If
possible, I'd like to keep it vague so I don't have to

But I find it hard to squeeze out even a half-hearted
lie when someone is staring straight at me like this.
"I'll answer that with a question...
Why do you want to know where I live?"

"Huh? But you asked me where my apartment was, didn't
you? I think it's unfair that I'm the only one who
doesn't know where you live.
Um... is that weird?"
"Well, it's a little weird.

Unfair, huh... That's a strange thing to get hung up

". It's not strange.

If I don't know where you live, I won't be able to
visit if something happens to you."
I stop chewing on my curry rice.

I feel like I just heard her say something that would
make any man happy.

"Visit me...? As in, if I catch a cold, will you come

"No, I won't.
At the moment, I have no intention of doing so."
I guess I was celebrating too early.
Senpai has no such intentions.

I see. In other words, she's just an airhead, isn't
she?

"My house is in the city too. It's about a
thirty-minute walk from here.

If you head up into the suburbs north of the station,
you know that residential area on top of the hill? It's
at the end of that."
"Oh, that's right. You're moving in today, right?"
Arihiko deliberately interjects.
Senpai tilts her head slightly.
"Moving in? Are you a transfer student?"
"Huh?"
Senpai says something strange.

Arihiko and I just silently make eye contact with each
other.

"Uh, Senpai... I joined this school as a first-year
student, and I've known you the whole time I've been
here.

What made you suddenly think that I'm a transfer
student?"
"Well, because you're moving―――"

"Moving doesn't necessarily mean I'm going to transfer.
I'm just changing addresses, not schools.

I've been living with my relatives up 'til now, but

After a look of surprised incomprehension from Senpai,

"So you just changed your address.

And now you've moved to a residential area in the
suburbs."

"That's right. To the ostentatious place at the top of
the hill."

"I see, that makes sense. Are you talking about the
Tohno mansion?"
Senpai asks hesitantly.

To the people from the city, the Western-style building
on the hill must be something special.

I haven't been back for seven years, but the Tohno
mansion in my memory is as big as a castle to me.

"Exactly. I know it doesn't really suit me, but now
that I've moved, it is what it is."

"Mmm, Seems like you aren't too enthusiastic about it

Guess you can't help it if you haven't been home for
seven years. It'll feel like someone else's for a
while, right?"

"I wonder. I haven't dropped by yet, so I don't really
know how it feels.

Well, if push comes to shove, I can always take shelter
at your house."

"Whaaaaat? Screw you, my house isn't your bivouac spot.
Thanks to you staying over every damn day you had off,
my sister's gotten more attached to   than she
is to me. My allowance has been dropping every year
since!"

I think that's probably more because of his bad
behavior, but I decide not to open that can of worms.

To be honest, I don't feel comfortable talking about
the Tohno family.
"Wow. You two are really close, aren't you?"

"We're not. He and I do compete with one another, but

mademoiselle."

"But he even stays at your house, doesn't he? That's

"That's not it, Senpai. He ran away just because he

bastard feels a bit guilty about being dropped on the

"So, he comes to me when I have a room available. My

Arihiko shakes his fist as if saying that he won't
forgive me.

I see... so that's why... I'll bring a souvenir or two

"As in... Tohno-kun was entrusted to the Arima family?"
Arihiko clams up, realizing he's said too much.
He puts on an uncharacteristically sheepish grin.

"Don't worry about it. It's not like it's anything to
be embarrassed about."

Without looking at Arihiko, I take another bite of the
curry rice.
"I see. Well, that's true.

Lightning would strike you down if you were to complain
about the time you spent there."

Arihiko nods his head, seemingly convinced. I think his
overwhelming optimism is a truly admirable trait.
"I'm sorry, Tohno-kun...

I mean, did you not get along with your previous
family...?"

"No, that's not true. This guy has no problems with the
Arima family. They're all super nice people. Well, Mr.
Arima himself is kinda scary, I guess.

And yet, he rejects any talk of becoming their adopted
child and runs away to my place during days off. What

"There's no reason for me to be dissatisfied with
anything. They've been good to me, I just don't want to
burden them anymore."
I finish my curry rice.

It's only a momentary lull though, and she quickly
returns to her normal cheerful expression.

"Habano-sensei was looking for you. He said he wanted
to talk to you about your place of residence."
"My place of residence? What, is this about my move?"
Habano-sensei is the head teacher of the second-years.

Since Toyama-sensei is absent, I guess this now falls
to him instead.
"Thanks, I'll head right over.

But... that's weird. I completed the procedures to
change my address yesterday."
I force my sluggish body to stand up.
Yumizuka stares at me motionlessly.
"Is there anything else?"
"Huh? N-No, there's nothing else, really!"
I wonder if Yumizuka is feeling sick as well.

At this point, Yumizuka Satsuki is one of the central
figures in our class.

She's cheerful, easy to get along with, hardworking,
and it's clear that she cares more about those around
her than herself.

I think most of the boys like her, and there are no bad
rumors about her among the girls.

Naturally, there's always a crowd of people surrounding
her.

She is a well-liked mood-setter, the polar opposite of
my unsociable self.

Although we're in the same second-year class, we've
only exchanged a few words.
To be honest, I'm surprised she even remembers my name.

"Tohno-kun. I was wondering if I could ask you
something."
"Sure. What?"
"Sorry if this is a weird question...

You just said you're moving, but are you going
somewhere else, Tohno-kun? Are you transferring to
another school?"
When she asked that question, I understood.

Her confusion is understandable, but her question is
off the mark.

"No, it's just a change of address. I'm only moving to
Souya. It's not a big change.

This is a good school, I wouldn't want to transfer
out."

"Y-Yeah, that's right! The entrance exam was super
tough! I studied really hard for it!"
R-Right.

Although, I wouldn't have thought someone like Yumizuka
would find this school particularly challenging.

"Oh. But Tohno-kun, if you're changing addresses, does
that mean you're leaving the Arimas?"

"Yeah, that's right. It's a shame I have to leave, but
I can't stay in their care forever―――"
No, wait a minute.

I'm positive that Arihiko is the only person who knows
that I've been living with the Arima family.
"I'm sorry. Did I ever talk to you about this?"

"Yeah, you told me all about it. It was a long time
ago, though."

"―――I see. I don't know what to say about
that―――"
I must have had nothing else to talk about.

I can't remember anything in particular, but if
Yumizuka and I were chatting like this in the past,
it's pretty plausible that I was struggling to keep the
conversation going and ended up mentioning it.

"Well, I'd better get going. Is Habano-sensei in the
staffroom?"

"Yes, he said he would dock you points if you didn't
show up in ten minutes. I wonder what points he's
docking exactly..."

Yumizuka laughs awkwardly, with neither sarcasm nor
irony.
I can't help but laugh as well.

Our school head has a habit of threatening to dock us
points, but 'poor conduct' obviously doesn't have any
impact on grades these days.
"By the way, what are you going to do for lunch?"

"I'll drop by the cafeteria on my way to the staffroom.
Arihiko will be there, after all."
"I-I see. See you later, Tohno-kun."

Waving awkwardly, Yumizuka leaves for her usual group
of girls.

After answering Habano-sensei's...  questions
about my relationship with the Tohno family as
succinctly as I could, I go to the cafeteria.

The cafeteria is busy again today. Most of the tables
are occupied, if not full.

Only about a third of students use the cafeteria. The
more budget-conscious among us tend to prefer the
school store, which is a bit cheaper.

Arihiko and I sit down at a table, watching the other
students line up with meal tickets in their hands.
Classes have ended.

I couldn't bring myself to head to the mansion right
away, so instead I've just been staring idly out the
window at the schoolyard.

The classroom has been dyed orange by the setting sun.
The color, like that of a still-wet watercolor red,
hurts my eyes just a little.
I don't really like crimson red.

Looking at it makes me feel nauseous. It's like it
seeps directly into the depths of my eyeballs.

As it turns out, I have a hard time with things that
remind me of blood.

Or more accurately, I've developed a condition that has
made me this way.

Seven years ago, Tohno Shiki had a near-death
experience.

I'm told that there was a terrible accident, and since
I happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time,
I was caught up in a collapsing building.

Initially, it had seemed that the injury would be
fatal, and everyone had given up hope. Apparently
things were looking pretty grim.

However, thanks to the quick response of the doctors
and the fact that all the wounds were concentrated in
one place, I was miraculously saved somehow.

When I think back on it like this, it seems like
someone else's story, and it's only natural that much
of it feels made-up.

One day, I unexpectedly got involved in an accident,
was struck by an object which pierced through my chest,
and lost consciousness.
I was like a machine that had been forcibly shut down.

My memories immediately following the accident are an
indistinct blur of pain and cold. The first thing I can
remember clearly is waking up in a hospital bed.
I still have the scars from that accident.

According to what I heard, not only did I land hard on
my back when I fell, but a piece of glass or something
had pierced my chest.

Thanks to that, I have a burn-like scar in the middle
of my chest and back.

The first time I looked directly at my body after the
wounds had closed, I passed out at the gruesome sight.

Since then, I've had frequent bouts of anemia and
fainted many times, causing a lot of trouble for those
around me.

That's probably the reason why my father――why Tohno
Makihisa left me with the Arimas. He must have thought
I wasn't strong enough to be the heir of the Tohno
family.
"A chest wound, huh..."
I hold back the wave of nausea that comes over me.

The pain is like a needle pricking my eyeball, but I
take some deep breaths and push through it.

That mark of death lies square in the middle of my
chest, hidden beneath my uniform.

Ever since that accident, I've been able to see the
'lines'.

Thanks to the glasses that Sensei gave me, I've been
able to live a decent life, but if I hadn't met her, I
would've lost my mind ages ago.

When I said goodbye to Keiko-san this morning, she was
concerned about the fact that the members of the Tohno
household are a little unusual.
She needn't have worried.
After all―――

Even if they are abnormal, I'm not exactly an ordinary
person either.
I put my glasses back on and pick up my bag.
I can't stay in the classroom forever.
I'll―――
I'll kill some more time.
There's no need to go rushing off.

It's not as if the situation is going to improve if I
spend all my time hurrying about.
I stroll aimlessly around the school.

There are almost no students in the building or on the
athletics field.

I'm glad that I haven't run into anyone I know, but
it's a bit eerie to see a place that's usually crowded
with people this quiet.
"Speaking of which..."

As I look around the empty athletics field, I remember
an incident from my middle school days.

It was a cold winter's day, and it was threatening to
snow. At the time, I'd been taking a shortcut across
the empty schoolyard.

When I heard noises coming from what should've been an
empty storeroom, I stopped by to see what was going on
and―――
"Hello. Are you a second-year?

I'm sorry, but can you please stay off the athletics
field after school?"
An upperclassman I don't know calls out to me.

I must have wandered onto the athletics field without
realizing it.

"I'm sorry, I was just going for a walk. I'll be more
careful in the future."

I apologize for my carelessness and step off of the
field.
"Were you not going home?"
"No, but I'm leaving now. Thank you for your concern."
I thank the upperclassman and leave the school grounds.
She's helped give me the kick in the rear I needed.

I'll just start looking suspicious if I hang around the
school any longer.

I'll go back to the classroom, collect my bag, and
return to my 'real home' this time―――
I walk a new route, back to my new home.

After passing block after block of close-knit apartment
complexes, I arrive at a spacious and upscale
residential area.
I'm getting closer and closer to the Tohno mansion...
The scenery around me isn't unfamiliar.

I lived in the Tohno mansion up until seven years
ago――until I was ten years old. My memories of back
then are definitely hazy, but this scenery is still
pretty nostalgic.
I'm not entirely sure how I feel right now.
This return trip is both nostalgic and novel to me.
I walk up a long slope.
There are fewer and fewer houses around.
―――The smell of greenery tickles my nostrils.

Even though we're in the middle of a city, the
atmosphere here feels like it has rejected modernity.

Almost all the land from this point on belongs to the
Tohno family.

The mansion where Tohno Shiki lived until he was ten
years old...

All it holds are old memories and a family that doesn't
get along.

Though, that said, I only have one immediate family
member left in the mansion now.

The father that hated me――Tohno Makihisa, the head of
the Tohno family, passed away the other day.
My mother died of an illness the year Akiha was born.

So, there are only two Tohnos left: me and my younger
sister, Akiha.

Normally, as the eldest son, Tohno Shiki would be the
family heir, but I've lost that privilege.

Being the heir of the Tohno family means being
subjected to a rigid education.

I hated it, so I'd always run off and go play. I can't
even remember how many times my father gave me a hard
time about it.

Then, I was involved in an accident that left me with a
physical defect, and he took the opportunity to cut me
off.

He said, 'Even if you're the eldest son, a weakling
like you who could drop dead at any time cannot be my
successor.'

I defied his expectations and managed to recover, but
by that time, my younger sister Akiha had been chosen
as the heir.

Akiha was already being raised as 'A daughter of the
Tohno family', but once I was out of the running, her
upbringing became even stricter.

I used to play together with her in the mansion gardens
up until I was ten years old――up until I was involved
in that accident. I haven't seen her even once since
then.
That was seven years ago.
I wonder how the Tohno mansion has changed.
I'll arrive at the mansion in a few minutes.

If there's one thing that's still on my mind,
it's―――

I think back on the time I spent with my father, Tohno
Makihisa.

To be honest... I don't actually remember doing
anything with him.

Makihisa was a strict father; a quiet man, who didn't
let his emotions show.

'Do not go outside. Do not go into the city. People are
born with different statuses. Protect our noble
bloodline. You shouldn't view yourself as the same as
other people.'

Those were Makihisa's rules, and by extension, the
rules of the Tohno family.
I rebelled against those rules.
I felt that my father's teachings were wrong.

Not because his reasoning was flawed; they just didn't
feel that convincing.

Maybe it was just me, but as a child, it felt like his
teachings didn't even belong in this ...

Although I wasn't the only one who disagreed with
Makihisa's words, I was the only one who could openly
defy him.

As a result, I began to ignore orders and would
frequently escape from the mansion. That's what led to
me being involved in the accident.

'The world outside the mansion is hideous. It is poison
to us.'
It's ironic.

My dad's favorite phrase ended up being true, even if
only for me.

After I woke up in the hospital, Makihisa didn't come
to visit me even once.

My final memory of him was him ordering me to 'go to
the Arima house' the day I returned to the mansion
after being discharged from the hospital.

I guess I'll never see that side of Makihisa again
either.

I think that the fact I'm not experiencing any strong
feelings about my father's death speaks volumes about
our relationship.
It's my sister Akiha, of course.

She apparently came to visit me a few times right after
I was entrusted to the Arima household.

Unfortunately, I didn't get to see her since I was
always on my way to and from the hospital. After she
went off to a boarding school, we only exchanged a few
letters.

Unlike Akiha, I'm no longer a member of the main
family.
That was why I was able to lead a free and easy life.

It wouldn't be inaccurate to say I've barely had any
contact with my sister at all these past seven years.

To be honest, the idea of returning to the Tohno
mansion hadn't even crossed my mind the entire time.
But Akiha is there.
When we were kids―――

She was quiet, and always followed me around as though
there was something out there that terrified her.

Perhaps it was her long black hair and luxurious
clothes, but Akiha seemed like a captive princess
straight out of a fairy tale. A fragile girl.

Even though I have no right to act like a big brother
now, I've been worried about her future these past
seven years.

Which is why when I heard the news of Makihisa's death,
my first concern was for her.

With our father gone, she was left all alone in that
vast mansion.

More than anything, I feel guilty about forcing the
duties of the Tohno family on her and living a selfish
life.

I think the reason why I agreed to come back to the
mansion may have been so I could apologize to her.

Come to think of it, there were lots of other people
living in the Tohno residence besides Makihisa and
Akiha.
Relatives of ours were staying in the main building.
Servants were living and working in the annex.

It was seven years ago, so I don't remember much, but I
do remember playing with other children, not just me
and Akiha.
I'm pretty sure they were―――
Damn, it's no use. I can't remember.

There were a lot of people coming and going at the
Tohno residence back then. I heard from Keiko-san that
seven years ago is about when Makihisa was vigorously
expanding his business.

Given how many strangers were showing up at the mansion
every day, it'd honestly be odd if I  remember each
and every one of them.

"Yeah, it probably wasn't important... Anyway, my
father's the reason I'm here now."
The main gate is firmly shut.

As a child, I knew that the Tohno mansion was 'pretty
big', but after living in the normal-sized Arima house,
it's finally sinking in just how huge this mansion
really is.

This entire hill overlooking the city is the property
of the Tohno family.

The plot with the mansion on it alone is larger than my
high school, and if you count the forest that spreads
out behind it, it's probably three times bigger.

The grounds are surrounded by a long wall and trees,
making it impossible to peek inside.

The main gate, which serves as the entrance to the
property, is closed and forbidding.

Next to the bigger gate for cars, there's a doorway for
people.

After a moment of hesitation, I press the button that
seems to be the doorbell.

Unlike a normal intercom, there is no ringing to be
heard by the person who pressed the button.

After a few seconds of waiting, the lock on the door
releases and the intercom buzzes, inviting me to enter.

"So the door's fully automatic now... There used to be
a guard."

I open the heavy door, pass through the stone gate, and
set foot on the Tohno estate.

The door locks tightly behind me with a satisfying
clunk.

Beyond the main gate, a gently sloping path leads into
the depths of the forest.

Tall trees hem in the path, making it feel like a
tunnel.

It extends due east, then after about forty meters
makes a hard left turn to the north.

With each step I take, my memories gradually start to
regain their luster.
I know this path.
I ran along it countless times.
Almost there.

At this corner, you turn north――to the left――and
there it is.

The Tohno mansion, towering high, like some imposing
castle.

I let out a sigh that could be of either admiration or
resignation.
It hasn't changed at all.

According to my father, the house was heavily renovated
after the war. The basic construction, however, was
inherited from my grandfather, who himself inherited it
from his own grandfather.

This is a castle for a powerful man. A man from a
family that has been in this land for hundreds of
years.

To Makihisa... no, to all members of the Tohno family,
this mansion is practically sacred.

At the annual family reunions, there would always be a
handful of adults trying to curry favor with my father
so that he'd rent them a corner of the mansion.

They were all probably successful businessmen with
their own mansions. Yet, for some reason, they were
obsessed with living here.

They must have considered living here to be very
prestigious.

What a bunch of nonsense... I'm not familiar with the
values of the upper class, so as far as I'm concerned
it's just a 'luxurious mansion'.
"Alright..."

There's no turning back now; not after I've come this
far.

Next to the double doors, there's an incongruous
doorbell.
I shake off my nervousness and push the doorbell.

The familiar ring that would usually follow never
comes.
The heavy silence continues for several seconds.

I can hear the sounds of hurried footsteps coming from
the other side of the door.
"Welcome, we've been expecting you."
Despite its heavy appearance, the door opens lightly.

I squint at the light of the setting sun shining
through the window.

I thought I'd prepared myself for this, but the sight
of the lobby is enough to take my breath away.

Any visitor would be overwhelmed by the architectural
beauty.

I get the striking feeling that I've been transported
to a different country in a different time. The
interior of the mansion is so dated that even the
atmosphere is different.

Still, this is the Tohno residence lobby of my
memories.

I stand there motionless, across from the person who
came to greet me――a girl in anachronistic clothes.

"Thank goodness. It was getting quite late, and so I
was starting to worry that you might have gotten lost.

If you hadn't arrived before dark, I would have left to
come find you."
The girl wearing a kimono and an apron laughs softly.
"Ah, no―――"

I'm so bewildered by this unexpected turn of events
that I can't speak coherently.

I'd assumed that the person waiting to welcome me would
have been the rugged-looking butler who had been
Makihisa's secretary.
"Hm?"

The girl tilts her head gently as if puzzled by my
confused attitude.
"You  Shiki-sama, right?"

"Y-Yes. Although, addressing me with a '-sama' is a bit
excessive."
"You are, right? Oh, please don't scare me like that!

You had me terrified that I might have gotten the wrong
person again!"

The girl in the apron presses her forefinger to her
lips with a warning gesture, like a mother scolding her
child.

It would appear that she really did worry and is now
quite cross. Even so, the smile remains on her face,
and she still gives off a welcoming atmosphere.
She's wearing a kimono and apron...

She came to greet me, and she addresses me as
'-sama'...
In which case, she must be―――
"Excuse me. Are you a maid here by any chance?"
She simply smiles in response to my question.
"You must be tired, right?

Please, come on in. Akiha-sama will be free to greet
you shortly, so please make yourself at home in the
living room until then."

The girl starts walking as if guiding me, her every
movement gentle and calm.

She heads toward the corridor on the east side of the
lobby, next to the grand staircase.

If I remember correctly, the door to the living room is
just inside that hallway.
I obediently follow her.

I may have lived in this mansion seven years ago, but I
was a child then. Although I remember some parts of it,
my memory is too vague to make sense of it.

I take a single deep breath and step into my nostalgic
family home.
And then...
"Oh dear. I've gone and done things out of order."

Whether she knows I'm nervous or not, the girl turns
around and bows politely.
"Welcome home, Shiki-sama.
I look forward to working for you."

Her smiling face really is like a flower in full
bloom...

Unable to come up with an appropriate reply, I timidly
follow her.
I decide to stop her and ask for her name.
I'd feel bad just calling her 'you there'.
"Excuse me, may I ask your name?

I've only just arrived, so I'm not familiar with
everyone yet."
I call out to her.
The girl in the kimono looks at me in surprise.

"My name is Kohaku. In this mansion, I serve the head
of the Tohno family."
Smiling, the girl bows after her introduction.

It was a gentle motion, like that of a flower blooming
from a bud.

Before that, I want to explore the mansion a little
more.

I know it's my own home, but seeing this elegant
mansion in the flesh has gotten me all excited.

"Excuse me. Before we go to the living room, do you
mind if I take a look around the other rooms? It's kind
of nostalgic."

There used to be a game room on the second floor of the
west wing...
"My, so you do remember it."
"But, my apologies.

The large rooms such as the game room, the library, and
the parlor have been locked since Akiha-sama became the
head of the family.

Even if you are the eldest son, you are not allowed to
use these rooms without her permission."
"Ah... I see. That's too bad."

She refuses me flatly. Having lost some face, I turn my
gaze away.

"I can't use the house quite so freely after all, can
I?"

"No, I am sure she will allow you to as soon as you
greet her.
Ah, but―――"

"It would be appreciated if you would ask permission
first before entering a locked room.

The Tohno residence doesn't just have security measures
on the outside, but on the inside as well. If you were
to enter any such rooms without approval, I wouldn't be
able to guarantee your safety."

"My safety? You're exaggerating, right? Are there going
to be darts flying at me?"
"No.

Something more terrifying than any darts――the thunder
of our strict master."

The maid smiles jokingly and once more goes to usher me
down the corridor.

I guess she wants me to go to the living room to rest
first.
"Welcome home, Shiki-sama.
I look forward to working for you."

Unable to come up with an appropriate reply to her
polite greeting, I timidly follow her.
The girl leads me to the living room.

The living room, which I haven't seen in seven years,
is so much more luxurious now that I feel as if I'm
seeing it for the first time.

I wonder if I've gotten too used to the Arima house, or
if the standards here have risen in these past seven
years.

Either way, I feel like this is a stranger's home, and
it makes me uncomfortable.
I start to look around the living room.
"... Cat got your tongue?

I understand how you feel, but please make yourself
comfortable. This is your home, after all, Shiki-sama."
"Y-Yeah, of course."
I hurriedly sit down on the sofa.

I only just came back to my own house, and I'm already
overwhelmed by everything. How pathetic.

The girl in the kimono moves the tea wagon located in
the corner of the living room closer, brews a cup of
tea, and brings it to me on a tray.
"It's nothing special, but here you go."
"Ah, thank you."

I can't help but feel embarrassed as she serves me
politely with a smile on her face.

I doubt it has anything to do with the way I lived at
the Arima house. I'm just middle class at heart.

"I must go and speak to Akiha-sama briefly, so please
sit tight for a moment.

It will probably take about ten
minutes, so you may want to look around the mansion
until then."

"Is it really fine for me to just wander around as I
please?"

"What are you talking about! This is your home now, of
course you are free to go where you please!

Ah, well, perhaps you had better avoid the second
floor. Akiha-sama is up there at the moment."

"Please feel free to look around as much as you'd like
so long as it is on the first floor.

It's been seven years since you've been to this
mansion. I'm sure you are feeling nostalgic and
excited."
She brandishes a mischievous smile.
"If you'll excuse me."

The girl, who I suspect is one of the maids here, bows
and leaves the room.
She brandishes a mischievous smile.
"If you'll excuse me."
Kohaku-san bows and leaves the room.
"I give up..."

The lavishly-made living room makes my muttering
reverberate even louder.
Should I stay here and pass the time being nervous?
Or should I take a walk around the mansion?
No, I'll wait here.

Walking around right after coming back is just going to
give me the jitters.
I should greet Akiha before I do anything else.
She's the current head of the Tohno family, after all.
I spend some time sitting on the sofa.

The view of the yard from the window matches what I
remember.

There's a courtyard the size of four tennis courts, and
a garden at the far end that seems ridiculous to even
measure.

On the other side of the garden, there are more woods,
and if I'm not mistaken―――

"Oh? I thought I'd stop by before leaving, but I didn't
know we had a prior guest."
I gasp and turn around at the sudden voice.

There, in front of the door leading back to the
lobby―――

Stands an all-black figure almost too strange to be
believed.
"Hello, Shiki-kun. Welcome to the Tohno residence...

Actually, that's not right. In your case, it would be
more apt to say  ."

The man――probably in his thirties judging by the
sound of his voice――saunters into the living room.
The fact that he is all-black is not a metaphor.

For whatever reason, he's covered in black bandages;
not only on his hands but all the way up to his face.

It makes him look like the central villain of the
archetypical mystery novel.
"Uh... who are you?"
"Hmm? You don't remember?
Ah, I see. It's me, Saiki Gouto.

We saw each other a few times when you were a kid,
albeit not like this. Even if you remembered me, you
wouldn't recognize my face."
Saiki...?
Was there a branch of the Tohno family with that name?

No, more importantly――this person is, how should I
say it―――

"It's alright, I'm used to people looking at me like
I'm a freak.

I burned my face in an accident. For a long time now, I
haven't been able to go outside without this getup.
Sunlight is especially harsh on me.

Akiha also dislikes it, but   . She is also
partly responsible for this, you know."

Saiki Gouto walks over to the trolley, makes himself a
cup of tea, and brings it to his lips.

It's an exaggerated gesture, but it doesn't seem out of
place.

It's a gesture of one born with natural dignity... a
casual elegance.

"But I must say... rather impudent to just return like
this."

"I'm talking about you, Shiki-kun. You broke Makihisa's
orders and escaped from the mansion, and as a result,
you were involved in a stupid accident and deserted."

"Deserted. Yes, deserted. You discarded your parents'
investment and abandoned your duty. Yet here you are,
back at the mansion, trying to act like Akiha's
brother.
Do you not feel ashamed of yourself?"

I almost leap to my feet, but check myself and lean
back into the sofa instead.

There's obvious contempt and provocation in Saiki
Gouto's eyes, but there's no point in making a scene
here. After all, there's no mistake in what he said.

"I do. Remember how you stripped down back when you

"Oh, did you forget? You changed in the kitchen before

Oh yeah...
I guess I did.
"Still, this comes as quite a shock.

"N-No, that was... you know, a force majeure, I just

and I was
just a teeny tiny bit curious, so I thought well, why
not..."

Senpai's frantically making excuses, but her face has

It seems like that's brought up memories of what she
saw back then.
Well, I'll just put that aside for now...

"A-Anyway, you won't have any objections so long as I

"Hmm... If the alternative is leaving you to your own

"Senpai!"

"However, you helping out Arcueid is the one thing I

The way she's behaving right now is utterly

"She's like...
a bomb?

I mean, it  impossible to predict what that lunatic

She's not exactly , right?

She doesn't do anything without a good reason to, and
the only thing she's done with her powers is defeat

"I wouldn't be so sure. Right now, her actions are

Her tone is indifferent, but it's clear from the look

What Senpai's saying is this:

Vampires are now the last thing the people in this city

Instead, they need to pray that this child leaves

"Th-That may be so, but―――

It's not like I act without thinking. I held myself

It's just... I could restrain myself when I was

"And so you lost your cool and fought her, huh?"
"I'm sorry...
I feel terrible about it now..."
Senpai curls up in shame.

I know I said that she was exaggerating, but I can

Arcueid definitely  acting strangely last night.

I made her angry too, so maybe I'd better step back and

"Very well.

You and Arcueid seem to be natural enemies, so I'll

I resist the urge to quip that birds of a feather
seemingly  flock together.

"I also won't initiate any contact with Arcueid either.
Not until she's calmed down first, at any rate.

In exchange, you'll search for vampires with me. How

"Uh? Ah, yes, that's... Huh?

Did you just say that you weren't going to search for

"It's basically the same thing, so don't overthink it.

Alright. It took some getting there, but it looks like

From this point on, I can work together with

Even if this time we have together won't last, being

With that matter taken care of, we settle into our more

We talk about inconsequential things while sipping on

About class. About the city. About our hobbies.

It's a peacefully mundane conversation, over the course

The bell rings, signaling the end of fifth period.

They say that time flies when you're having fun, but I

"We probably shouldn't  skip sixth period, huh?"
I get up off my floor cushion.

As I put my left foot forward on my way to carry the

My vision flickers in and out.

My consciousness and vision bleed together like two

The feeling fades from my limbs, and I start hurtling

I slip into the sort of coma I've experienced far more

Senpai catches me just before I completely collapse to

"Sorry... I got a little dizzy.

"I  worry about it! Please don't try to put on a

Senpai hurries over to the kitchen.
It seems like trying to act tough will only worry her.

I don't really want to lie down on the floor, though...
I'd feel pathetic if I did that in front of Senpai.

Instead, I lean my back against the wall and slowly

Now that I'm sitting comfortably, the dizziness has

I'm glad I didn't pass out...

If that was the worst of it, then it shouldn't be long

As I'm resting against the wall, I hear the bell ring

It seems like the ten-minute break between classes is

"Looks like we'll miss sixth period after all, huh."
I didn't even notice Ciel-senpai sidle up next to me.

She peers at me as though trying to gauge how healthy I

"I've brewed some ginger milk tea that's chock-full of
honey.

"Thank you very much..."
I thank Senpai and take the proffered teacup. It's hot.

I'd honestly been craving some cold water instead, but
as soon as I take a sip―――

"Ah! Senpai, this is amazing! Just one mouthful was

"Of course! This recipe was handed down to me by my

Senpai puffs out her chest as though she'd come up with

The pungent zesty smell of the ginger, the smooth

I drink the entire cup without even realizing it, after

Not because I'm exhausted, but because I've reached a

Now that I think about it, I've been stressed out ever

I guess I relaxed a bit after reconciling with Senpai,

The warm tea has helped to alleviate my symptoms, and I

"I know that this is scandalous to suggest as your

"Yeah, probably.
I'm not living on the edge like Arihiko."

"Inui-kun must be quite the character for you to talk

I'm a little envious."

Out of concern for my health, Senpai doesn't try to

She simply sits by my side, silently drinking tea,

Time ticks by, but the silence isn't oppressive.
On the contrary, it feels pleasant.

Senpai and I just stay like this, not touching, but

"By the way, Tohno-kun...

We don't have anything to do, so how about a game of

"Absolutely not!"

Where the hell did that idea come from?! Also, way to

"And why shiritori, of all things?!

"I do, Tohno-kun. You strike me as the sort of person

Where'd she get that idea? I almost started crying

"I-I want to play it even less when you ask with that

I refuse to play shiritori. If you don't have anything

"What a shame. Very well, I'll keep on plotting how

"Geez... You're weirdly childish in some ways, or maybe

I tilt my head back, let out a sigh, and close my eyes.
Still... her teasing was kinda fun.

I never thought I'd get the opportunity to banter with
Ciel-senpai like this.
"Tohno-kun...? Did you fall asleep?"
"I'm awake. I'm just resting my eyes for a second."

"I see. In that case, just ignore me and make yourself

I'll take her up on that offer and lie down for a bit.

I allow my back to slowly slide down the wall I'd been

I must have been lying here for about ten minutes or so

At this rate, I actually will fall asleep, so before I

"So... Why shiritori?"

"You seem like you're always forcing yourself to stay

You're even doing it right now, aren't you? Even though

You probably have for the past seven years...

you understand that if you close your eyes, there's no

That I felt that way is something I never spoke of,

I said that vampires were frightening.
That fighting to the death was frightening.

To me, it is these mundane days that entail a constant

The fear that my precious time on this earth won't last

Nothing is more painful than having to accept that

"Hey now, that's not true at all. I'm pretty healthy

But I can't let myself put that fear into words.
Fear leads to jealousy and hatred.

I have to suppress the part of me that fears the

Because, when it comes right down to it, I'm alive.
I don't want to let the eyes through which I see the

I let out a soft sigh, blinded by the light streaming

I'm incredibly reassured by her words, and I think I've

I don't feel the same way about Senpai as I do about

"Is that right?

I banish the insecurities that nearly escaped my lips,

I pick myself up from my semi-supine position and take

"By the way, Senpai, as a little taste of your own

Senpai?!

Will she take me with her, or will she refuse, and in

Provided I follow her instructions...

Meaning that she'll protect me with all her strength if

It's a callous way of doing things, but I can't fault

All she's doing is implicitly telling me just how

I'll do as Senpai says...

Even though Arcueid said that Roa is already dead, that

'A vampire's lair is rigged with traps to foil would-be

If that's true, then as an amateur, I'd be more

"I understand. It's alright if I just wait here,

"Of course. However, if I'm not back in under an hour,

Senpai hurries out of the tea ceremony room without

.........It's been about an hour.
Ciel-senpai still isn't back yet.

She's the last person I'd expect to find herself in

What if, hypothetically, remnants of the Dead still

Not a problem.

Senpai could easily take on even a hundred of the Dead

What if, hypothetically, she came across Arcueid?
